name: Question 14
problem: The position $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,t⟩,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=\pi \,\text{s}.$
worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at $t=\pi ,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,1⟩, \\ v(\pi ) & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at $t=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩, \\ a(\pi ) & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v(\pi )\cdot a(\pi )$ and $||v(\pi )||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\pi )\cdot a(\pi ) & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,0,\,0⟩ \\  & =0, \\ ||v(\pi )|| & =\sqrt{(0)^{2}+(1)^{2}+(1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at $t=\pi ,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v(\pi )\cdot a(\pi )}{||v(\pi )||} \\  & =\frac{0}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is $0\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$

Question 14
?

The position r, in meters, of a particle P at time t is given by r(t)=⟨cos⁡t,−sin⁡t,t⟩, where t is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of P at time t=πs.

a
2ms−2
b
2ms−2
c
22ms−2
d
0ms−2
e
1ms−2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The tangential component of acceleration is given by aT=v⋅a||v||.

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at t=π, as follows: v=⟨ddt(cos⁡t),ddt(−sin⁡t),ddt(t)⟩=⟨−sin⁡t,−cos⁡t,1⟩,v(π)=⟨−sin⁡π,−cos⁡π,1⟩=⟨0,1,1⟩

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at t=π: a=⟨ddt(−sin⁡t),ddt(−cos⁡t),ddt(1)⟩=⟨−cos⁡t,sin⁡t,0⟩,a(π)=⟨−cos⁡π,sin⁡π,0⟩=⟨1,0,0⟩

Then, we compute v(π)⋅a(π) and ||v(π)||: v(π)⋅a(π)=⟨0,1,1⟩⋅⟨1,0,0⟩=0,||v(π)||=(0)2+(1)2+(1)2=2

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at t=π, and we get aT=v(π)⋅a(π)||v(π)||=02=0.

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is 0ms−2.
